A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SmartEraser work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. All 11 pages of each were inspected. Neither contains an appendix; the supplementary material mentioned in Section 3.2 is absent from both supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–3, a 30-participant user study in Table 4, and component ablations in Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, user-study outcomes and component ablations, with revised numerical results in several tables.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same full-image/mask conditioning, synthetic copy-and-paste pipeline, six mask augmentations, CLIP/MLP visual guidance and diffusion training objective.

E1.justification: Both use the same Syn4Removal training sources and evaluate on RORD-Val, DEFACTO-Val and Syn4Removal-Val. The real-world examples with user-provided masks also retain the same scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain ZITS++, MAT, LaMa, BLD, RePaint, SD-Inpaint, CLIPAway and PowerPaint. The user study and real-world comparisons retain the same LaMa, CLIPAway and PowerPaint subset.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark construction, approximately 5,000 samples per benchmark, six metrics, training settings and inference mask dilation are unchanged. Both user studies specify 30 participants, 20 image sets and randomized presentation. No protocol revision is reported to explain the changed scores.

E4.justification: Both retain the cumulative RG, ME and VG ablation in Figure 8/Table 5 and the same user-mask case analyses in Figure 7. The ablation questions and comparisons are unchanged; the numerical revisions are assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Both report metric point estimates and user-vote proportions without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: All 31 FID entries across Tables 1–3 and 5 change, revising quantitative margins and baseline rankings. SmartEraser FID changes from 10.901 to 16.030 on RORD-Val, 3.496 to 3.405 on DEFACTO-Val, and 2.634 to 4.386 on Syn4Removal-Val. RORD-Val's best FID baseline changes from LaMa to PowerPaint. Table 2 also changes SmartEraser's ReMOVE from 0.949 to 0.939. SmartEraser remains best on every reported metric, and the cumulative ablation trend is retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same objectives, feasible pasting regions, blending formula, mask transformation, visual conditioning and diffusion loss. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about Masked-Region Guidance, the million-triplet Syn4Removal dataset, and superior object-removal quality and robustness.

C2.justification: The explanations of object-regeneration prevention, context preservation, training/testing mask mismatch and component benefits are retained. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added, and the discussion is not revised to explain the numerical updates.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same SD v1.5 fine-tuning configuration, trainable modules, AdamW optimizer, batch size 32, 500,000 iterations and learning rate 2e-5. Dataset-construction details and the project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 55 references and related-work positioning are retained. Reference-list differences concern page backlinks and reflow, without added works or revised novelty relationships.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in the introduction and Section 3, revised author affiliation/contribution markers, and an added project-leader credit. The section hierarchy and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same eight figures and five tables are retained. Figure 5 moves from page 6 to page 5, Figure 6 moves from page 7 to page 6, and Tables 1–2 change from side-by-side placement to stacking in the right column. Spacing and typography also change, without new visual analyses.

improvement.justification: The dominant change is the unexplained replacement of numerical scores; the PDFs do not establish whether their accuracy improved. A reporting inconsistency also results: Section 4.2 retains a 10.3-point RORD-Val FID advantage, matching the earlier PowerPaint gap of 10.326, while v2 Table 1 gives 8.028. With the experiments and conclusions otherwise retained, the limited editorial changes and unresolved reliability of the revised scores do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
